question.problem: Find the solutions of the equation $25{z}^{2}+36=0.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}25{z}^{2}+36 & =0 \\ 25{z}^{2} & =-36 \\ {z}^{2} & =-\frac{36}{25}\end{aligned}
$$

By taking square root, we obtain:

$$
z=\pm \sqrt{-\frac{36}{25}}
$$

We now rewrite $z$ using the imaginary unit $\text{i}=\sqrt{-1}\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\pm \sqrt{-\frac{36}{25}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{36}{25}\cdot (-1)} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{36}{25}}\cdot \sqrt{-1} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{36}}{\sqrt{25}}\cdot \sqrt{-1} \\  & =\pm \frac{6}{5}\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
